messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Single-storey rear extension of 20 m2 with a flat roof", "project": "Semi-detached house in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "Sch 2 Part 6 para 1", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(1) A detached single storey building, having a floor area which does not exceed 30m2, which contains no sleeping accommodation and is a building— (a) no point of which is less than one metre from the boundary of its curtilage; or (b) which is constructed substantially of non-combustible material."}, {"ref": "para 2.2", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.2 Part P applies to electrical installations: a. in a dwelling-house or flat, and to parts of the installation that are: (i) outside the dwelling – for example fixed lighting and air conditioning units attached to outside walls, photovoltaic panels on roofs, and fixed lighting and pond pumps in gardens (ii) in outbuildings such as sheds, detached garages and domestic greenhouses. b. in the common access areas of blocks of flats such as corridors and staircases c. in shared amenities of blocks of flats such as laundries, kitchens and gymnasiums d. in business premises (other than agricultural buildings) connected to the same meter as the electrical installation in a dwelling – for example shops and public houses below flats."}, {"ref": "para 2.3", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.3 Part P does not apply to electrical installations: a. in business premises in the same building as a dwelling but with separate metering b. that supply the power for lifts in blocks of flats (but Part P does apply to lift installations in single dwellings). NOTE: Schedule 2 to the Building Regulations identifies buildings – for example unoccupied, agricultural, temporary and small detached buildings – that are generally exempt from the requirements of the Regulations. However, conservatories, porches, domestic greenhouses, garages and sheds that share their electricity with a dwelling are not exempt from Part P (by virtue of regulation 9(3)) and must comply with its requirements."}]}

message.content:
An ordinary 20 m² single-storey extension to a house is building work that needs a building notice or full plans application.

- **Not exempt.** The Schedule 2 Part 6 exemption quoted covers only detached single-storey buildings. An extension attached to the house does not qualify. The Class 7 exemption for small attached structures (not quoted, but relevant) covers only conservatories, porches, covered yards and carports, not a normal extension.
-
message.reasoning: This 20m2 rear extension on a semi-detached house doesn't qualify for the Class 7 exemption since that only covers conservatories, porches, covered yards, or carports under 30m2—a standard flat-roofed extension isn't exempt, and since it's not detached, it falls under building notice or full plans. As a dwelling, the Fire Safety Order doesn't apply, though I'm unsure whether it's near a sewer or on a private street since that wasn't specified.
